profile.headline: Software Engineer
profile.summary: Full-stack software engineer specialized in front end development with expertise in Javascript, Python, React, Django, Flask, and more.  Learn more about me at leehplance.com

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
- Designed and built Go/gRPC microservices from the initial commit — founded our policy (system-of-record for all insurance policies), task, and sequencer services; built and own our accounting/billing service end-to-end; delivered the initial build of a fifth.
- Build cloud-native microservices with Go, gRPC, Protocol Buffers, PostgreSQL, and Kubernetes, communicating across an event-driven architecture (RabbitMQ).
- Built tooling to automate Django migration generation, cutting repetitive manual work in the team's development workflow.
- Maintain availability and reliability of services in production Kubernetes; partner with the SOC team to remediate dependency vulnerabilities proactively.
- Partner with Product to ship features and resolve issues across an insurance platform spanning policy, billing, and rating.
- Work across GCP — IAM, Secret Manager, Artifact Registry, Cloud SQL — in support of GKE-deployed services.

- Designed and implemented  features to provide validations when giving assignment extensions to students.
- Fixed issues/bugs of existing Django codebase on collaboration with team members.
- Wrote unit and integration tests for newly added features to maintain 100% test coverage.

positions.title: Research Associate
positions.description: Worked as a research associate. Responsible for executing well-designed experiment and involving in parts of designing process. Also in charge of part of administrative and accounting process.

positions.title: Undergraduate Researcher
positions.description:
-Researcher, Department of Molecular, Cell and Developmental Biology
My studies in the laboratory of Dr. Sanford involve elucidating how disease-causing mutation in pre-mRNA exon can affect alternative splicing.

• Problem: Investigating of alternative splicing activity caused by disease-causing single nucleotide mutation on pre-mRNA exon.
• Approach: Create plasmid containing beta-globin reporter gene along with wildtype or mutated exon, in order to perform splicing assay.
• Contribution: Designing wildtype and mutant exon, Cloning of exon into reporter plasmid, Extraction of RNA from mammalian cells, and Splicing assy.
• Conclusion: Some disease-causing mutations in exon can alter pre- mRNA splicing. This is possibly result of creation or deletion of exonic splicing enhancer (ESE) or exonic splicing silencer (ESS).
